text:
Close the 340K proxy-cache cliff leak (R20a-c)

Problem (2027-01-09 cache round 5, HIGH): post-R12, 47 requests still crossed the ~340K litellm proxy cache ceiling at 16.3% hit (340-400K bucket: 83.7% resets; daily maxP reaches 408,956). R13 (fill_rate 0.3 + the 340K ceiling minus a 32,768 margin → effective trigger ~300K on 1M-window GLM endpoints) did NOT prevent over-cliff prompts.

Root cause (three stacked gaps, code-verified):
1. Rule-4 skip: when the conversation ends in an open tool loop spanning back to messages[1] (a long single-turn tool run — exactly where context grows fastest), summary_cut_index retreats the cut to the loop start and summarize returns messages UNCHANGED (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338, 437-485); maybe_compact falls through and the request is sent at full size.
2. No send-gate: when compaction runs but cannot shrink below the threshold, the code explicitly continues (src/agent/turn.rs:1743-1750 — "Still over: the kept-verbatim tail dominates..."); the 5-attempt budget aborts only on the 5th attempt, so up to 4 over-cliff requests go out per turn, and the next turn resets the budget.
3. Tokenizer drift: the trigger counts cl100k BPE tokens; the provider counts GLM tokens (~10% higher on code-heavy content) — a 300K-cl100k conversation can be 330-345K provider tokens, and one iteration's tool results plus GLM reasoning echo (policy: never strip) jumps past the trigger between checks.

Fix instructions (R20, three parts):
a. Send-gate at the cliff (src/agent/turn.rs maybe_compact ~:1660-1760): when the pre-request count is still over the proxy ceiling after the compaction attempts, do NOT send the full prompt — either (i) allow under-pressure historical-reasoning stripping for GLM as a cliff-pressure exception (the under_pressure machinery exists at src/provider/openai/request.rs:54 and DeepSeek uses it; GLM's never-strip policy blocks it — src/provider/policy.rs), or (ii) fail the turn fast with an actionable error instead of burning up to 4 over-cliff requests.
b. Trigger margin for 1M-window endpoints (src/config/general.rs:334/343 defaults; src/agent/context.rs:151-163 trigger math): lower the effective trigger to ~280K (fill 0.28 for 1M windows, or ceiling 320K) so tokenizer drift plus one tool batch cannot jump past the cliff.
c. Rule-4 fast-fail signal: when summarize no-ops because the open tool loop spans the conversation AND the count is over the ceiling, return a "skipped: open loop" signal from summarize/summarize_with_interrupt (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338) so maybe_compact surfaces "context over the proxy cache ceiling inside an open tool loop — finish or interrupt the tool run" immediately instead of silently re-sending.

Acceptance: a regression test where a conversation over the ceiling inside an open tool loop fails fast (or strips under pressure) instead of sending >340K; no post-fix request_stats row exceeds the ceiling (verify via the aggregates extraction); cargo test --workspace green with the existing compaction tests updated to the new behavior.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-cache-hit-5-review.md (HIGH-1, R20); .coding/analysis/cache-hit-5-aggregates.txt (A3/A4 buckets); executive summary BUG 4.
note: Closed 2026-11-11 (lead clean-up): obsolete. The LiteLLM proxy-cache ceiling was removed from compaction triggering, and no configured endpoint runs through a LiteLLM proxy any more (DeepSeek, Ollama Cloud, Kimi).

text:
Move API keys to the OS keychain

Problem (2027-01-09 security review, LOW, optional): endpoint API keys sit plaintext at rest (endpoints.toml / ~/.mnemo/keys.toml) — DACL-restricted on Windows, 0600 on Unix. An OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain) would tighten at-rest storage. Worthwhile AFTER the .git/ sandbox-escape item lands (that one is the actual escape hatch).

Fix instructions:
1. Add an optional keychain backend for endpoint secrets: on load, if a key is referenced as keychain:<name>, fetch it from the OS store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain via the `keyring` crate or equivalent) instead of the file.
2. Keep file-based keys working (default unchanged — no forced migration); add a settings action to migrate a key into the keychain.
3. Multi-platform neutrality: the crate must support both Windows and macOS (the project's review expectation) — `keyring` v3 does.
4. Tests: a mocked keyring backend round-trip; config load with keychain: references; cargo test green on both platforms.

Acceptance: a key stored in the OS keychain is used for requests with no plaintext on disk; file keys still work; cargo test --workspace green.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-security-review.md (LOW-3).
note: Decided 2026-11-11: keep, deferred — do it as its own plan after Mnemo1 is retired, so the key storage changes in one settings surface (Mnemo2 Endpoints) instead of two.

text:
Persistent session context — durable resume without loss

The agent session's CONTEXT (the transcript + the resume-relevant session state) lives in memory only: a shutdown loses the conversation unless the caller exported a transcript themselves. Durable today: plan files (.coding/plans/<id>.md — the crash-resumption doc) and memory_write facts; NOT durable: the conversation and the spawn settings. The resume seam already exists but nothing persists to it — a caller must build `SpawnOptions { resume: Some(Transcript { messages }) }` (src/headless/types.rs) by hand and thread the same model/permissions/limits to reconstruct the session.

Problem to solve: with the option ON, every session durably snapshots at turn boundaries + park/end so ANY point is resumable without loss; with the option OFF, zero new disk writes and today's behavior is byte-identical.

Fix direction:
(1) Config option `persist_context` (default false — behavior-preserving) in the [general] section, src/config/general.rs (follow the compaction_survival pattern around :776), surfaced as a toggle in the GUI options dialog (the Settings pages + the config IPC).
(2) Persistence hook at turn end / park / session end: serialize Transcript + the resume state (model, permissions, limits, host_tools specs, external_policy spec) into the state dir (e.g. <state>/sessions/<session-id>.json) via the existing export machinery — `AgentSession::export_conversation` + `snapshot()` (src/headless/session.rs; §5.9.5 snapshot/pending in .coding/design/headless-free-agent.md).
(3) An Engine-side restore surface (e.g. `Engine::saved_sessions()` / `Engine::resume_session(id)`) that rebuilds SpawnOptions from the snapshot and spawns with `resume: Some(...)` — the initial_messages threading already exists in spawn_agent_shared (src/host/runtime.rs:73-289).
(4) Multi-platform: pure Rust + the existing config/IPC surfaces — no platform-specific paths (the state dir comes from Workspace.state_dir).

Acceptance criteria:
- Scripted-provider integration test (tests/integration/headless_kernel.rs pattern — RecordingLlm + opts(Workspace, cfg)): with the option on, run a turn, DROP the engine, start a fresh engine on the same state dir, resume the saved session, and assert the model's first request carries the prior messages + the spawn settings round-trip.
- With the option off: no new files appear under the state dir and all existing tests stay green.
- The toggle is visible in the options dialog and takes effect for NEW sessions (documented).
- Full workspace battery green (cargo test, exit 0, zero warnings under #![deny(warnings)]).

Pointers: memory "PLAN: Job 3c resume — D3 mid-step" (the manual state-save pattern this automates); master spec .coding/design/headless-free-agent.md §5.9.5 + §5.3 (resume); the transcript export (AgentSession::export_conversation) and spawn threading (src/host/runtime.rs:73-289).
note: Decided 2026-11-11: keep — plan it for 2.4 as a Mnemo2/headless-engine feature, after 2.3 ships.

text:
Finish should tick appended review-fix steps

Problem (2026-10-21, live case plan 8813e7ab): a plan that goes through review rounds ends Complete with its appended fix steps still rendered as open checkboxes. `.coding/plans/8813e7ab.md` shows `- [x]` on steps 1-7 and `- [ ]` on steps 8-13 — the six steps `update_plan append=true` added in Reviewing for the review findings H1-H4, L1-L4 and the verify/commit step — even though the work shipped (commits 36e7a74, e2729c8, 6219ec9 on wt/mnemo) and review round 3 returned `## Verdict: PASS` (.coding/reviews/2026-10-21-8813e7ab-toolcard-labels-review-round3.md). Anyone reading the plan frame sees six open items on a completed plan.

Cause: `complete_step` is hidden in the Reviewing state by design (a reviewer-driven fix must not rewrite plan progress), and the sanctioned fix-scoping path (`update_plan` with `append=true`) produces steps that stay unchecked "through the exit" per the workflow lifecycle text.

Fix direction: when a plan finishes — the `finish` tool's handler on the transition into Complete — mark every still-unchecked step of that plan as done in the frame, or move appended review-fix steps into a distinct `## Review fixes (done)` section with its own state. Keep every step's TEXT (the frame is the crash-resumption document; never drop them). Anchors: `src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs` (the `finish` and `update_plan` handlers) and `src/app/workflow/plan_file.rs` (the plan-frame writer that renders `- [x] N.` / `- [ ] N.`); the lifecycle sentence that documents the current behaviour is in `src/agent/prompt.rs` (WORKFLOW_LIFECYCLE, the Reviewing-adjacent text).

Acceptance: a plan whose listed steps are all complete, with two steps appended during Reviewing, run to Complete must render with no unchecked step (or the appended pair under the done section), and `current_plan` / the plan pane must agree with the frame. Regression test in the plan-tool tests (plan.rs / plan_file.rs): finish a plan carrying appended unchecked steps, assert no `- [ ]` remains; the red-check on today's code shows the six `- [ ]` lines.

Pointers: memory SPEC "chat tool cards — one human headline per run" (plan 8813e7ab) and its round-3 PASS report; `.coding/plans/8813e7ab.md` itself is the reproduction fixture.
note: Closed 2026-11-11 (lead clean-up): Mnemo1-only. It is about Mnemo1's workflow Finish/plan-file checkboxes, which retire with Mnemo1; Mnemo2's plan board ticks steps on team_merge / plan_step_done and does not close a plan with open steps. | plan loop did not close (workflow: Complete) — item left in_flight; work kept in tree; run waits for the plan to close (the next turn resolution re-checks) | steered by the user, kept in flight — the plan stays active, resume to continue | steered by the user, kept in flight — the plan stays active, resume to continue | steered by the user, kept in flight — the plan stays active, resume to continue | steered by the user, kept in flight — the plan stays active, resume to continue | steered by the user, kept in flight — the plan stays active, resume to continue

text:
OpenSpec support: current-state specs, spec deltas on plans, schemas and a Settings > Specs page

Spec: .coding/design/openspec-support.md (read it first; written 2026-11-04 with the user).

Adopt OpenSpec's file formats, not its tool: current-state specs in openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md (Requirement/SHALL + WHEN/THEN scenarios), plans carry ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED spec deltas, closing a plan merges them and writes an OpenSpec archive folder (close is gated on clean deltas). Support OpenSpec schemas (schema.yaml artifacts, templates, instructions, config.yaml context/rules) as plan sections and dispatch gates, with a Settings > Specs page to pick, add, fork and edit schemas. Backlog gets a "Plan this" button. Start with the dispatch-routing and tier-ladder capabilities. Plan after unified tiers (87932c46); three open questions are at the end of the spec.
note: Done 2026-11-11 (lead clean-up): landed earlier — OpenSpec format layer + requirement indexing (2db26453), spec deltas on plan_create, Settings → Specs page in Mnemo2.

Stop 'missing-test' mistakes for good (seen in 3 reviews)

The same kind of review finding keeps coming back:
- argShape1: No end-to-end test of a text line range through the real file_edit tool (src/agent/tests.rs)
- missExcerpt1: The excerpt-bearing multi_edit funnel path is tested only with a hand-written error string (src/agent/dispatch.rs)
- rcptShift1: Untested branches: deletion above a cite, the insertion-inside message, file_write mint-write-cite (src/tool/agent/read_registry.rs)

Suggested enforcement: a test or check that catches it. Plan this to add the guard, then cite it in the finding's category so later reviews can check it.
